question.text: A sample of a radioactive nucleus <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> disintegrates to another radioactive nucleus <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo></math> which in turn disintegrates to some other stable nucleus <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi><mo>.</mo></math> Plot of a graph showing the variation of number of atoms of nucleus <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> vesus time is : (Assume that at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></math> there are no <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> atoms in the sample)

solution.text:
No. of nuclei of B is initially zero and finally zero.
It will reach a maximum value at some intermediate
time.
